limits.description: Legal hemp cultivation exists in Serbia (fibre, seed and further-propagation use, THC capped at 0.3%, requiring Ministry of Agriculture authorisation), but according to CMS Expert Guides, "the extraction of CBD oil is not regulated by law" and Serbia's Commission for Psychoactive Controlled Substances has given an opinion that CBD itself is a psychoactive substance capable of unwanted effects.

notes: This is genuinely ambiguous, not a confirmed personal-import rule — sourced to a law firm's country guide (CMS Expert Guides) and a hemp-industry site (Hemppedia), not Serbia's own regulatory text read directly. Given the Commission's stated position, don't assume a CBD product is safe to bring into Serbia just because it's legal where you bought it; treat it with the same caution as cannabis until you've confirmed current status with Serbian authorities. Moved to UNVERIFIED on 2026-10-17: the only sources are a law-firm guide and a hemp-industry site.

legal_source.name: CMS Expert Guides — Cannabis Law and Legislation in Serbia

limits.description: Since around August 2020, Saudi Customs has banned individuals from importing e-cigarettes, shisha and their accessories through shipping companies and personal website purchases — goods imported this way are confiscated, a fine is imposed, and a seizure record is registered. Companies licensed by the Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) may still import these products in commercial quantities.

notes: This measure is specifically about shipping/mail-order/online-purchase import channels for individuals — it does not clearly say whether it also restricts what a traveler personally carries in accompanied luggage, and that distinction wasn't confirmed either way in this pass. Don't assume it's safe to bring a personal vape in checked or carry-on baggage just because this rule targets shipping specifically — but also don't assume accompanied baggage is covered by the same ban. Corroborated identically across 5 independent outlets (Saudi Gazette, Zawya, Al Bawaba, Riyadh Xpress, Vaping Post); every direct fetch of the Saudi Gazette article itself returned HTTP 402 (paywalled), so this is strong multi-source corroboration rather than a directly read primary article. Separately, Arab News (directly fetched and quoted) traces the same underlying policy back further: the Ministry of Commerce and Investment banned e-cigarette/vaping sales in September 2015, and "considers anyone bringing them in from abroad to be smuggling" — broader phrasing than 'shipping only' — so the individual-import restriction isn't a one-off report, it's a long-standing, consistently-described policy, even though the accompanied-baggage question specifically remains unresolved. Domestic sale/possession has separately been legal since Royal Decree 38621 (2019) — don't confuse 'legal to own in Saudi Arabia' with 'legal to personally import.' Moved to UNVERIFIED on 2026-10-17: the cited source is a newspaper (Saudi Gazette); ZATCA's own announcement wasn't read.

legal_source.name: Saudi Gazette — 'Customs ban individuals from importing electronic cigarettes' (c. August 2020)

limits.description: General Administration of Customs Announcement No. 102 of 2022 (effective 1 November 2022) allows passengers to duty-free carry 2 e-cigarette devices plus 6 cartridges/liquid products totaling 12ml or less. Travelers on Hong Kong/Macao routes get a lower allowance (1 device, 3 cartridges, up to 6ml); frequent cross-border travelers get less still (1 device, 1 cartridge, up to 2ml, once per day). Travelers under 16 may not carry e-cigarettes at all.

notes: The announcement number and exact figures are corroborated identically across multiple independent Chinese sources (news outlets, tax-law reference sites, industry sites) — a direct fetch of customs.gov.cn itself still fails on a self-signed certificate, the same block this project has hit on Chinese government domains throughout, so this is strong search-corroboration rather than a directly read government page. Moved to UNVERIFIED on 2026-10-17: the figures were corroborated by news and reference sites; customs.gov.cn returns 412 to our fetches.

limits.description: Drones over 250g must be registered with Brazil's civil aviation authority (ANAC) through the SISANT system, which requires a Brazilian CPF or CNPJ taxpayer number — the real obstacle for tourists, who would need to obtain a CPF from a Brazilian consulate beforehand or have a Brazilian resident register the drone on their behalf. Drones of 250g or under don't need registration for recreational use, but must still follow altitude, visual-line-of-sight and people-distance rules.

notes: A direct fetch of ANAC's registration page was blocked by a CAPTCHA in this pass, so this is drawn from consistent secondary reporting rather than the primary page's own text — treat the CPF/CNPJ barrier as the well-corroborated headline fact, but re-verify against ANAC directly before treating exact figures as final. Moved to UNVERIFIED on 2026-10-17: the facts came from secondary reporting; ANAC's page is behind a CAPTCHA.

legal_source.name: ANAC (Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil) — Cadastro de Drone (SISANT)

A new IMANOR product safety/labeling standard for smoke-free products takes effect February 2026.

notes: Confirmed via consistent reporting across 7 independent Moroccan financial/business press outlets (Le Desk, La Vie Éco, H24info, Le360, Médias24, and others), not a direct Morocco Customs (douane.gov.ma) fetch — that domain and its specific circulars are bot-blocked from this environment. limits.description: Kenya's e-cigarette import status is actively contested in court, not settled. Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale announced a directive on 31 May 2025 suspending the manufacturing, importation, distribution, sale and promotion of nicotine products and requiring all existing licensees to reapply. On 4 June 2025, Justice Bahati Mwamuye of the High Court issued a conservatory order — following a petition by Susan Awino — restraining the government "from implementing or enforcing the decision suspending all licences and import clearances," pending full determination of the case. A separate, broader ban announcement is also reported for 30 July 2025.

notes: No Kenya Gazette notice was found for either the ban or the court order — this is reported only through Kenyan mainstream press (The Standard), not a government-primary document. Given the active litigation, don't treat either 'banned' or 'allowed' as settled — check current status before relying on this for travel planning.
summary: Uncertain: a 2025 government suspension of nicotine-product imports is on hold under a High Court order.

legal_source.name: The Standard (Kenya) — 'Court halts CS Duale's ban on nicotine product licences and importation'

limits.description: Albania's tobacco-control law (Law No. 9636, as amended through 2024) defines "smoking" to include electronic cigarettes, and permits their retail sale (18+ only) subject to restrictions — but the law's provisions found in this pass are about domestic manufacture, marketing and retail-sale channels (e.g., a ban on selling tobacco products, including via the definition covering e-cigarettes, "through the postal service"), not a traveler-facing import quantity.

notes: The Customs Authority's own traveler duty-free page (used for the tobacco and alcohol allowances above) does not mention e-cigarettes, vapes, or e-liquid at all — unlike tobacco, there is no stated personal duty-free allowance or explicit ban for travelers bringing a vape. Domestically, nicotine liquid may only be placed on the market in refill containers up to 10ml or disposables up to 2ml, with nicotine concentration capped at 20mg/ml — whether this domestic market-placement rule is enforced against a traveler's personal device wasn't confirmed. Treat this as unresolved rather than clearly allowed or banned.
summary: E-cigarettes are legal in Albania for adults; the law sets no traveller import limit.

legal_source.name: Law No. 9636, dated 6.11.2006 "On the Protection of Health from Tobacco Products" (as amended through 2024)

limits.description: Not named specifically, but falls under the Customs Authority's blanket ban on importing "plants, narcotic medicaments and psychotropic substances of natural or synthetic nature, their materials and their preparations" — the same provision covering cannabis generally.

notes: Moved to UNVERIFIED 2026-10-26: the CBD verdict was an inference from the Customs Authority's general ban on narcotic plant preparations; no Albanian page names CBD. No Albanian government page found that names CBD specifically or draws a distinction by THC content, unlike some countries' customs authorities. Given the blanket wording covering cannabis-plant preparations generally and no confirmed exception, treat CBD products the same as cannabis: do not bring them. This inference (CBD swept in under the general cannabis/narcotic-plant provision, not a CBD-specific rule) should be treated as somewhat less certain than the cannabis row itself.
summary: Treated as banned: CBD isn't named, but Albania's customs ban on narcotic plants and their preparations covers cannabis products.
